name: cadiz-resiste/openrta-tools

why_useful: Companion/earlier version of the OpenRTA pipeline above; committed JSON snapshots give a point-in-time cut of the same Andalucía STR registry usable without re-querying the API.

name: bc-report-2024
what_it_holds: R/ and output/ folders for the lab's 2024 British Columbia STR report (province-wide, following BC's short-term rental legislation). No data/ folder visible in the top-level tree (likely pulls from a private DB), so this is analysis code, not a committed dataset. Sibling repos bc-report-2022 and bc-report-2023-summer are the same report series in earlier years.
why_useful: One of very few GitHub repos referencing a BC-wide STR analysis, relevant to gap #12 (Vancouver/BC STR registry); worth an authenticated follow-up read to see if it ingests the BC provincial short-term rental registry launched under the Short-Term Rental Accommodations Act.
themes: Canadian and Australian STR registries and datasets (Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal, Quebec CITQ, BC registry, Sydney NSW STRA register, Melbourne)

Point-in-time provincial STR supply/growth report (BC has had aggressive 2024 STR legislation); figures alone give visual time series but no machine-readable numbers were found committed.
Recency is notable (2024 report on BC's new province-wide STR law) -- relevant to gap #12 (STR ordinance tracker) as a pointer to a fresh regulatory-impact study, though no data is committed.

Shows the lab publishes an annual province-wide BC STR report; the code/methodology could be reused even without the underlying (likely proprietary AirDNA-sourced) data, and any published PDF/output linked from it may contain BC-wide STR volume estimates useful as an external benchmark.

BC's 2024 STR law was one of the most aggressive North American regulatory shocks to STR supply; this is a direct, academically-produced measurement of its effect, useful for the Canada component of NA regional mix and as an analogue for how other jurisdictions' registration laws might bite.

name: passport-index-data
what_it_holds: 7 files (1 JSON + 6 CSV: matrix/tidy x name/ISO2/ISO3) of visa requirements for 199 countries x 199 destinations (visa-free days, visa-free, visa-on-arrival, eTA, e-visa, visa-required, no-admission); actively maintained, most recent data dated 17 Feb 2026; MIT licensed; 83 stars, 4 commits; explicitly the maintained continuation of ilyankou/passport-index-dataset which is now archived (last updated 12 Jan 2025)
why_useful: Currency of a passport/visa-openness index is a proxy for ease of cross-border travel by nationality pair; can be joined with regional nights mix (gap 7/20) to test whether visa-liberalization events move bilateral travel flows into ABNB's regional splits. This is the live successor to the widely-cited but now-archived ilyankou repo.
time_coverage: current snapshot only (no historical panel in this repo)
themes: Cross-border and visa data: Schengen visa statistics, ESTA, ETIAS, CBP wait times, passport index, border crossings BTS
